hydro_fact: Hydro-Québec reports 152.672 TWh of hydropower generation in 2025 and 37.371 GW of total installed generating-station capacity (all source types).
hydro_scale_comparison: A 100 MW continuous load is 876 GWh/year, about 0.57% of Hydro-Québec’s 2025 hydropower generation; this is a provincial scale comparison.
grid_and_policy_fact: Hydro-Québec says data centres currently use about 200 MW and could exceed 1,000 MW by 2035; projects over 5 MW are selected, and a proposed C$0.13/kWh rate is subject to regulatory approval.
municipal_water_fact: Montréal reports 1.6 billion litres/day produced from the St. Lawrence, Lac Saint-Louis and Rivière des Prairies; this is city-wide production, not unallocated industrial capacity.
screen_assessment: Strong provincial hydro and urban water context; a 100 MW connection would still require utility selection and a site-specific grid study.
open_question: Quebec City and Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean are alternate corridors to screen; municipal water capacity and firm transmission for a specific campus are not established here.

hydro_fact: Manitoba Hydro reports 6.074 GW net generating capability across its system, with nearly all annual electricity generation from 16 hydro stations; most hydroelectric output comes from northern stations.
hydro_scale_comparison: 100 MW is about 1.65% of Manitoba Hydro’s 6.074 GW net generating capability; this compares nameplate capacity, not uncommitted supply.
grid_and_policy_fact: The 2025–26 annual report says drought reduced hydro generation and required larger power imports; that is a reminder that hydro output and exportable surplus vary with water conditions.
municipal_water_fact: Winnipeg's water-treatment plant is designed for 400 million litres/day; this is plant design capacity, not free cooling-water allocation.
screen_assessment: Strong hydro/water resource screen and a major urban service base; regional transmission and drought-adjusted firm supply need confirmation.
open_question: A 100 MW campus is about 1.6% of Manitoba Hydro's reported generating capability; this comparison does not imply 100 MW is uncommitted or deliverable in Winnipeg.

hydro_fact: BC Hydro generated 40.860 TWh from hydro in fiscal 2025; hydroelectric installations account for over 80% of BC Hydro's installed generating capacity.
hydro_scale_comparison: A 100 MW continuous load is 876 GWh/year, about 2.14% of BC Hydro’s FY2025 hydropower generation; it would also equal one quarter of the 400 MW maximum allocation in the 2026 call.
grid_and_policy_fact: BC Hydro's 2026 emerging-industries call allocates up to 400 MW province-wide to storage and AI data centres, showing that hydro-richness does not mean spare local capacity is available to any one project.
grid_and_policy_source: BC Hydro 2026 Call for Demand Q&A
municipal_water_fact: Prince George reported 11.333 million m³ of water supplied in 2023 (about 31.1 million litres/day on average), drawn from municipal groundwater wells; this is an annual average, not a guaranteed new industrial allocation.
water_source: City of Prince George 2023 water-system report
screen_assessment: Hydro-rich provincial system and a city water network make this a candidate for screening, but BC Hydro's allocation process and regional transmission are material constraints.
open_question: A 100 MW campus would consume about 2.3% of Prince George's 2023 average municipal water production at the 0.3 L/kWh planning WUE; confirm seasonal source yield and permits.
